title: Qwen 3.8-Flash-Next (qwen4_exp): GDN MoE with 512 experts top-10 plus shared, hyper-connections, n-gram PLE table, sparse indexer attention

recommended.why: the sparse indexer is the family's attention; forcing dense past its budget is a diagnostic arm, not a lane to ship

with a cache above auto, wiring the slots turned a loss into a win (at auto itself wiring is noise, +1.8%) on decode: s96 wired +6.7% and s128 wired +16.9% against auto while s96 unwired lost 2.7% in the same sweep; tokens identical. Opt-in: it takes 6-10 GB more than auto out of the system's reach, so it is a setting for a machine with that much free, not a default

the default without wiring. Re-swept on real text: auto (48 slots, 66% decode hit rate) beat unwired s96 by 18% and s128 by 15% and s64 was noise at +2.1 GB; larger caches cut expert I/O but the host's GPU wait grew from 29 to 47-49 ms per token with GPU busy time flat, because the larger slot memory churns through the macOS memory compressor (about 5M pages per run at 96 slots, near zero at auto)

findings.conditions: offline replay, not a speculative run; the numpy port is unverified against the reference beyond its acceptance (95% first-row acceptance on math says the features and port are right); one greedy path per prompt; priced as tau x 84.2 ms / (C(b) + 5 ms) with C from qwen4exp.verify-cost-curve-real-2026-10-31 and the 5 ms drafter cost an estimate
findings.note: acceptance is good (the drafter card reports 2.8-3.3 at block 4 under sampling on the FP8 target), the speedup is not: verify rows stream their own experts, so even perfect drafts cap at about 1.3x at block 4. The lever is expert I/O, not drafting

findings.workload: tslab sweep --baseline sauto@auto/auto --candidate s64/s96/s128@N/streamed: protocol medium-review (426 prompt tokens), 64 decode, context 2048; 3 clean pairs per candidate, 0 dirty
findings.conditions: verdict records: s64 noise 1793463977496-82579-44, s96 loss 1793463977500-82579-45, s128 loss 1793463977505-82579-46; effect floor 3.49% from null record 1793463217525-58186-16, whose baseline-again arm itself won +6% while decode ran 11-12 tok/s against 16-17 tok/s in the sweep (page cache warming between the two commands), so the floor came from a colder host; swap rose from 2.2 to 3.7 GB during the s128 warmup and stayed there; phase values are medians over the sweep's runs from the decode_phases block. The cause of the extra GPU wait is memory compression of the slot pages: QWEN4_EXP.md section 'Why larger expert caches lose (2026-10-31)'

findings.workload: tslab sweep --baseline sauto@auto/auto --candidate s96w@96/streamed:expert_slots_wired=1 --candidate s128w@128/streamed:expert_slots_wired=1 --candidate s96@96/streamed: protocol medium-review (426 prompt tokens), 64 decode, context 2048; 3 clean pairs per candidate, 2 of 26 runs dirty
findings.conditions: verdict records: s96w win 1793466278644-9099-52, s128w win 1793466278647-9099-53, s96 loss 1793466278651-9099-54; no null run in this experiment, so the floor is the 2% default (the 3.49% null floor from qwen4-slots-real is below every win's lower bound); s128w's upper bound comes from one pair whose auto run read 13.7 tok/s; decode digests identical across all 26 runs; swap held at 6.7-7.5 GB from other sessions; wired arms still compress other pages; plain s96 lost 2.7% here against 18% in the earlier sweep, so the unwired loss depends on host memory state; the memory allowance is exceeded by design (6-10 GB growth)
findings.note: the wired slot pages are taken from the rest of the system for the process lifetime

findings.workload: tslab sweep --baseline sauto@auto/auto --candidate sautow@auto/auto:expert_slots_wired=1 --candidate s64w@64/streamed:expert_slots_wired=1: protocol medium-review, 64 decode, context 2048; 3 clean pairs per candidate, 2 of 17 runs dirty
